newsitem.title: USA: U.S. 1996 agro exports to top $60 billion - Glickman.
newsitem.headline: U.S. 1996 agro exports to top $60 billion - Glickman.

text.p: U.S. agricultural exports will top the $60 billion mark in 1996, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said on Saturday.

"We just got the news that agricultural exports will hit all-time record levels -- $60 billion this year," he said at Farm Aid '96, a benefit concert designed to raise funds and public awareness of the problems facing U.S. farmers.
Glickman admitted farmers still faced problems, but he said there were positive developments too.
In the last two years, farm assets had increased faster than farm debt, Glickman said. Low interest rates, low unemployment and low inflation rates were benefitting farmers.

One out of every three acres of production in the United States went to crops headed for export, he said. At the same time it was essential that small and medium-size farmers shared in the export market, he added.

Glickman took part in a town meeting where farmers from across the nation expressed concern about the growing concentration of large industrial-sized farms, which they said were forcing small family farmers out of business.

"While I don't like the structure problems of agriculture, when you've got more and more larger producers the fact is this year we will see net farming income of $51.5 million. It's never been higher," Glickman said.

Rhonda Perry, a Missouri farmer, called on Glickman to block funding of a $25 million dollar swine research centre in Iowa, saying: "We don't want taxpayer funded research that subsidizes factory hog farms."
Country and Western singer Willie Nelson later kicked off Farm Aid '96, the ninth benefit concert for the farmers.
Nelson, Neil Young, John Mellencamp and Hootie and the Blowfish headlined the all-star show, which drew more than 45,000 music fans.
Since the first concert in 1985, Farm Aid has granted nearly $13 million to more than 100 farm organizations, churches and service agencies in 44 states.
